items.title: Eddie Marshall interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 8, 2002
items.q: we had what we used to call the Boss of the Street, Mr. Griffin, who was like in the black mafia or something

ctx.x: Right. Well it’s nice to have that on your side, isn’t it.

Oh because I see so many guys that their parents were just like totally against it, this is a bad idea, and I thought boy. But I mean I started playing professionally when I was 14. But it was always with relatives. I had to get home. Even when I worked with Cookie, we had what we used to call the Boss of the Street, Mr. Griffin, who was like in the black mafia or something, you know numbers, writers and all this kind of stuff. And he made sure I got home every night, every night. It was funny. I remember one…
He knows how to take care of himself I guess.
